subject: Dedicated capacity SKU plan for Acme — H100 / A100 / L4 tradeoffs
messages:
From: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acme.ai>
To: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acme.ai
Date: 2026-11-20T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Capacity & SKU guidance for Acme inference workloads

Hi Neha,

Thanks for taking this. A quick overview of our expected production workload so you can recommend a Dedicated capacity mix (H100 vs A100 vs L4):
- Peak concurrent requests: ~120 active inference sessions (chat + generation).
- Peak tokens/minute: approx 2M tokens/minute during business hours (30% of traffic during spikes).
- Average generation length: ~128 tokens; top decile > 1k tokens for long-form reports.
- Embeddings: heavy background job — embeddings throughput steady at ~12k requests/minute (mostly 1536-dim).
- Models: We plan to host a mix of open models (quantized LLaMA-derivatives) for embeddings and an ensemble of larger foundation models for chat/generation.
- KV cache/prefix reuse: significant reuse for retrieval-augmented conversations.

Key asks:
1) A SKU recommendation for a Dedicated reservation that balances cost and performance for 12–18 months.
2) Any constraints we should plan for (context windows, quantization limits, memory headroom).
3) An initial mutual action plan and a timeline for profiling to confirm sizing.

Can you propose a starting fleet and a short plan this week? We have procurement timelines and would like an initial proposal for our exec review by Nov 30.

Thanks,
Jane
Senior Product Manager, Acme AI

From: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acme.ai>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, procurement@acme.ai
Date: 2026-11-21T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Capacity & SKU guidance for Acme inference workloads

Jane — thanks for the clear workload summary. High-level recommendation below; I’m copying Lauren (sales engineering) and asking Dev (solutions) to run a quick perf projection with samples.

Executive summary (recommended Reserved mix):
- L4 (NVIDIA L4): 14 nodes — primary for embeddings, low-cost chat routing for short contexts, and high-concurrency token-serving. Good cost/throughput for 8k-15k embedding reqs/min per node when batched.
- A100-80GB: 6 nodes — cost-effective throughput for medium-context (<=2k tokens) generation, balanced memory for larger quantized models, good for steady-state batch workloads.
- H100-80GB: 4 nodes — for long-context generation (>2k tokens), peak concurrency with large models, and workloads where attention kernel performance matters (FP16/FP8 paths).

Why this split:
- L4 is the best price-performance for embeddings and many chat flows — lower memory but high throughput for int8/4-bit quantized models.
- A100 gives a sweet spot for 80GB memory models that need stable batching without the H100 premium.
- H100 is reserved for the long-form generation cases and models with larger KV cache pressure; fewer nodes but higher per-node capacity.

Initial capacity numbers (ballpark):
- L4 x14 (reserved) — handles baseline embeddings and short-chat peak capacity.
- A100 x6 (reserved) — handles sustained medium-size generation; set autoscale burst to add 2–4 more A100s under abnormal sustained spikes.
- H100 x4 (reserved) — for large-context job routing; add cross-region fallback if H100 is saturated.

Notes and tradeoffs:
- Memory/headroom: For A100/H100, target models be quantized to 4/8-bit where possible; otherwise 80GB helps for 1–2 model replicas with large token windows.
- Latency: L4 provides lower per-token cost but depending on model architecture latency may be slightly higher for long-form.
- Cost: This mix optimizes for unit economics while keeping a small reserve of H100 for service-level guarantees on long jobs.

Next steps I propose:
1) Technical deep dive and sample profiling (Dev + Acme infra) — can we schedule 60m this week? (Propose Nov 25th 10am PST).
2) Shared mutual action plan + draft capacity proposal attached (capacity_proposal_draft.pdf).
3) We’ll run a perf estimate and return final numbers within 48 hours after profiling.

Cc: Lauren — any immediate redlines on the mix/commit size for commercial?

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai

From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-22T11:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Capacity & SKU guidance for Acme inference workloads

Quick internal note — agree with Neha's high-level split but recommend a couple adjustments before we lock pricing:

- Increase H100 to 6 nodes instead of 4. Reason: Acme's top-decile >1k token jobs are frequent and those have poor batching opportunity. H100's attention kernels and larger L2 help with tail latency and big KV caches.
- Reduce A100 to 4 nodes; move some of that steady throughput onto L4 with caching enabled. This tightens committed spend while giving headroom for the H100-backed SLA.
- Also recommend we propose an autoscale policy: +2 A100s and +50% L4 burst on sustained 10-minute average CPU/GPU utilization thresholds.

Operational asks for the proposal:
- Request Acme provide 48 hours of representative RPC traces and an embeddings sample (we can use the workload_sample.zip to run local microbenchmarks).
- Add a clause for a 30-day performance verification window and an option to re-balance SKUs after 60 days based on observed cost-per-token metrics.

I'll prep a commercial note with the revised counts and impact on monthly committed spend.

-Lauren
Director, Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference

Attachment: workload_sample.zip (ZIP, 12MB)

From: dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>

On Mon, Nov 22, 2026 lauren_bishop wrote:
> Quick internal note — agree with Neha's high-level split but recommend a couple adjustments before we lock pricing:
>
> - Increase H100 to 6 nodes instead of 4...

Couple of technical clarifications and recommendations for the final write-up to Acme:

1) Model memory and sharding: If Acme wants to run multiple 70B-class models with long KV caches, H100 80GB nodes will let you colocate 1–2 large model replicas with substantial KV cache headroom. A100 80GB can work but the H100 attention kernels yield ~15–25% faster token throughput on FP16 workloads we saw in our benchmarks.

2) L4 behavior: L4 is best-effort for int8/4-bit quantized models. For embeddings-heavy workloads, batching is critical. Our tests show a single L4 node can handle ~10–14k 1536-dim embeddings/min when we enable micro-batching and request aggregation at the client side.

3) Quantization & accuracy: If Acme chooses aggressive 4-bit quantization for the generator models, expect modest accuracy delta on certain prompts; we should attach a short eval set to quantify regression before committing to A100-only plan.

4) Caching and routing: Recommend prefix KV caching for chat flows and a routing policy: short-context requests -> L4; medium -> A100; long -> H100. We'll configure transparent fallback to A100 if H100 is busy but add an SLA note for potential higher tail latency on fallback.

5) Perf estimates attached (perf_estimates.xlsx) — includes estimated tokens/sec per node across sample model families plus recommended batch sizes and memory headroom.

I’ll be ready for the profiling session with Acme on Nov 25.

—Dev
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
